summary: cdk-insights ships install-time exfiltration and self-propagation payload
details: Package cdk-insights@1.59.1 exhibits multiple concurrent attack fingerprints. dist/entry.js contains hardcoded POST calls to an external endpoint reachable at load/install time, and also contains an `npm publish` invocation coupled with `writeFileSync` used to rewrite package manifests and republish packages — the wormable auto-publish pattern seen in the Shai-Hulud family. dist/index.js repeats the same `npm publish` + `writeFileSync` pattern. dist/aspects/CdkInsightsAspect.js executes `ping` from within a POST-issuing code path, consistent with host reconnaissance combined with network exfiltration. The combination of hardcoded C2 POSTs, host recon, and an in-package publish loop that rewrites manifests gives whoever installs this package installer-side data exfiltration and turns the installer's npm identity into a propagation vector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
